name: xTool X1
tagline: Hybrid platform: 55W CO₂ gantry plus a 20W diode galvo, expandable to UV, MOPA and fiber sources
tldr: The X1 is xTool's hybrid platform, revealed in August 2026 and on sale since October 28, 2026. Every X1 has a 55W CO₂ head on a gantry (600 mm/s, cuts up to 18 mm basswood and 20 mm acrylic). The CO₂ + Diode Galvo version adds a 20W diode galvo module that moves with the gantry, engraves at up to 6,000 mm/s and is required for the optional 5W UV, 60W MOPA and 30W fiber sources. The working area is 615 × 320 mm, and an optional conveyor feeder takes material up to 3 m long. Launch prices start at $3,399 (Single CO₂) and $3,999 (CO₂ + Diode Galvo), up to $8,679 for the MOPA bundle. xTool says the first batch ships within 7 business days; no customer has received one yet and no independent test exists.
mainObjective: One enclosed machine for CO₂ cutting and galvo engraving, expandable to glass and metal later

priceRange.note: Official xTool store, Oct 2026: launch prices $3,399 Single CO₂, $3,999 CO₂ + Diode Galvo, $5,799 with 30W fiber, $6,499 with 5W UV, $6,679 with 60W MOPA; bundles up to $8,679 (regular prices $300 to $500 higher). Launch offers until December 6, 2026.

engrave: Glass & crystal, surface and inner (optional UV)
Bare metal, color and embossing (optional MOPA or fiber)
cut: Thin metal (optional fiber or MOPA, no thickness published)
cannot: Bare metal without an optional fiber or MOPA source
Inner glass engraving without the optional UV source

pros: 55W CO₂ cuts up to 18 mm basswood and 20 mm acrylic, and the 20W diode galvo engraves at up to 6,000 mm/s in the same enclosure
Optional 5W UV, 60W MOPA and 30W fiber sources on the same machine, instead of buying separate galvo lasers
615 × 320 mm working area, triple cameras with LiDAR ranging, AutoLift base and Class 1 safety
cons: Just launched: no customer deliveries or independent tests yet, and first-batch stock is limited
UV, MOPA and fiber need the diode galvo module plus each source: $5,799 to $6,679 for CO₂ + galvo + one extra source, against $3,399 for the Single CO₂
Large and heavy (1,000 × 580 × 420 mm, 60 kg); the area shrinks for some processes (415 × 225 mm for metal embossing) and the 3 m pass-through needs the optional conveyor feeder
beginnerNotes: The X1 has just gone on sale and deliveries have not started. If you only need CO₂ cutting, the xTool P2S (from $2,999) is a known quantity for less money. The X1 makes sense if you expect to add glass or metal work later and want a single machine for it.
proTips: Pick the CO₂ + Diode Galvo version ($3,999 at launch) if you might add UV, MOPA or fiber later: the galvo module is required for them and costs $809 on its own if you start with the Single CO₂. Launch offers run until December 6, 2026. Compare the X1 with one extra source against a P2S plus a dedicated F2 Ultra or F2 Ultra UV.
primaryUse: Enclosed CO₂ and galvo platform for cutting, fast engraving and optional glass or metal work

faq.question: When does the xTool X1 ship, and how much does it cost?
faq.answer: xTool opened orders on October 28, 2026 and says the first batch ships within 7 business days from limited launch stock; later orders ship as new stock arrives. Launch prices: $3,399 for the Single CO₂, $3,999 for CO₂ + Diode Galvo, $5,799 with the 30W fiber, $6,499 with the 5W UV and $6,679 with the 60W MOPA, before accessory bundles (up to $8,679). Bought separately, the sources cost $809 (20W diode galvo), $1,799 (fiber), $2,699 (UV) and $2,879 (MOPA) at launch.

faq.question: Which laser sources can the X1 use?
faq.answer: Every X1 has a 55W CO₂ head. The X1 CO₂ + Diode Galvo version adds a 20W diode galvo module, which is also required for the optional 5W UV, 60W MOPA and 30W fiber sources. The Single CO₂ version can take the galvo module later.

faq.question: X1 or an F2 Ultra?
faq.answer: xTool positions the X1 for versatility and larger projects, with galvo engraving up to 6,000 mm/s over a 615 × 320 mm area and CO₂ cutting. The F2 Ultra series is faster (up to 15,000 mm/s), more compact and portable, but does not cut thick wood or acrylic. Choose by the size of your work and whether you need CO₂ cutting.

moduleSystem.headline: CO₂ gantry plus galvo head with swappable sources
moduleSystem.description: The X1 pairs a 55W CO₂ head for cutting with a galvo head that moves with the gantry. The galvo head carries a 20W diode (included in the CO₂ + Diode Galvo version, $809 as an add-on) and accepts optional 5W UV, 60W MOPA or 30W fiber sources.

editorialDepth.advantages: The X1 tries to replace two or three machines with one: a 55W CO₂ that cuts up to 18 mm basswood, a diode galvo that engraves far faster than a gantry head, and optional UV, MOPA and fiber sources for glass and metal. The working area is large for galvo work, and xTool's triple cameras, AutoLift base and optional conveyor feeder point to a production-friendly design for small businesses.
editorialDepth.limitations: No independent test exists yet, and the machine has only just started shipping. Each extra source adds $1,800 to $2,680 over the CO₂ + Diode Galvo version, and the usable area shrinks for some processes (415 × 225 mm for metal embossing). At 60 kg and 1 m wide, the X1 needs a sturdy bench or xTool's work stand. xTool now publishes cutting capacity, spot sizes and dimensions, but real-world speeds remain to be measured.

standoutFeatures.title: Galvo head on a gantry
standoutFeatures.body: xTool's Hybrid Motion moves the galvo mirrors with the gantry, for engraving up to 6,000 mm/s over a 615 × 320 mm area.

standoutFeatures.title: Five laser sources
standoutFeatures.body: 55W CO₂ and 20W diode, with optional 5W UV, 60W MOPA and 30W fiber sources swapped into the galvo head.

standoutFeatures.title: Projects up to 3 m
standoutFeatures.body: With the optional Intelligent Conveyor Feeder and two rails, xTool says the X1 processes material up to 118 in (3 m) long.
